problem: Build a growing skill library that supports new manipulation tasks while retaining performance on previous tasks under restricted historical demonstration access.
contribution: LOTUS combines continual skill discovery with hierarchical imitation learning and experience replay; a meta-controller selects skills and latent subgoals from an expanding library.
algorithm: Segment demonstrations temporally using DINOv2 feature similarity, pool segment features and form initial spectral clusters using silhouette-selected cluster count. Assign incoming segments to existing clusters above a silhouette threshold or add a new skill. Finetune skill policies and a hierarchical meta-controller with exemplar replay.
observations: Workspace and wrist-camera image histories, proprioception, BERT task-language embeddings and latent subgoals; DINOv2 features are used for discovery.
actions: Task-space manipulation commands from goal-conditioned skill policies; transformer/GMM heads model multimodal actions. Meta-controller predicts a skill index and subgoal, not actuator-safe instructions.
embodiment_and_data: LIBERO-OBJECT10tasks, GOAL10 and50selected kitchen tasks; real MUTEX50tasks with25base tasks followed by5stages of5tasks. Real base tasks use30demonstrations, incoming tasks10; retain5demonstrations per task.
experiments: Simulation20trials/task repeated over3randomseeds; compares full method, replay-free variant and discovery/vision-backbone ablations. Real-robot evaluation reports aggregate lifelong metrics; per-task real evaluation denominators not extracted from examined main text.
baselines: Sequential finetuning, flat experience replay, adapted BUDS, LOTUS-ft without replay; CLIP/R3M versus DINOv2 discovery features; no-new-skill ablation.

quantitative_result.value: LIBERO-OBJECT AUC LOTUS65.0±3.0 versus ER49.0±2.0; NBT11.0±1.0 versus24.0±0.0, mean±standard error over3seeds,20trials/task. These are aggregate success-derived percentage metrics.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p6 TableI and experiment text
quantitative_result.caveat: The paper's FWT definition p3 uses completed-stage diagonal performance, unlike LIBERO's epoch-averaged learning-curve FWT; matching names do not ensure matching formulas.

limitations: Requires expert teleoperation and retention of previous demonstrations; memory burden grows with thousands of tasks. Skill similarity/clustering thresholds and finite maximum skill-index capacity matter. A learned library does not automatically establish zero-shot composition on unseen tasks or another robot.
code_and_license: Primary paper retrieved and read. Executable code pin and code license were not verified in this review; implementation reuse requires a separate audit.
hardware_adaptation: Use as an explicit continual skill-composition baseline only after recording actual skill policies, checkpoints and replay budget. Explorer's symbolic BFS skill composition is engineering glue, not an implementation of LOTUS's learned cVAE meta-controller.
algorithm_detail: The goal-conditioned low-level policy jointly learns an encoder for look-ahead image subgoals. The high-level cVAE is trained from cluster skill labels and subgoal embeddings; logits for uncreated skills are masked to negative infinity before softmax. Existing skills use new partitions plus stored exemplars, and the replay buffer retains partition membership.
integration_contract: Store each skill's policy checkpoint, embodiment/action/camera contract, data partition and pre/postconditions. Track whether a sequence is a symbolic proposed plan, trained hierarchical policy, simulator execution or physical execution. Keep replay-budget and cluster-version metadata.
license_evidence: Code license UNKNOWN; primary paper is not permission to copy an uninspected implementation.
required_experiments: Matched flat replay versus hierarchical composition with equal demonstrations/memory; no-new-skills and no-replay ablations; held-out task combinations; all-prior-task retention after each update; real per-task attempted/success/unknown counts and intervention costs.
difference_from_explorer: Growing skill libraries, replay and meta-controller composition already exist. A task graph that returns skill IDs is useful scaffolding but does not reproduce learned hierarchical lifelong manipulation.
